skill.name: python-web-app-security-audit
skill.description: Run defensive pre-release security tests for Python web applications. Use for FastAPI, Django, Flask, and ASGI services: the common interface between Python web apps and servers. Tests authentication, authorization, hostile input, headers, CORS, cookies, rate limits, errors, and configuration to return evidence-backed findings and clear test boundaries.
skill.summary: Run configurable defensive pytest checks for Python web applications before release.
skill.author: glenskii

security_audit.summary: All 123 static findings are false positives in context. They describe documented test configuration, bounded file copying, in-process HTTP checks, defensive payloads, or Markdown code examples; no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious commands, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Test credentials and application settings are loaded from .env.test.
remediation.suggestion: Use dedicated non-production accounts, keep .env.test out of version control, and limit file permissions.

remediation.issue: The preparation helper copies a bundled security directory into the target project.
remediation.suggestion: Review the source and destination before running the helper, and preserve its refusal to overwrite an existing security directory.

remediation.issue: The suite checks only configured application behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Pair the suite with dependency scanning, production HTTPS and proxy checks, infrastructure review, and application-specific CSRF tests where applicable.

content.user_title: Audit Python Web Apps Before Release
content.value_statement: Python web teams need repeatable checks for common application security failures before release. This skill runs configurable pytest checks and returns evidence-backed findings with clear test boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Runs configurable pytest checks against local FastAPI, Django, Flask, and ASGI applications.
Tests authentication enforcement and account enumeration resistance.
Checks authorization boundaries, object ownership, and mass assignment behavior.
Exercises hostile input, malformed payloads, type coercion, headers, CORS, and cookies.
Checks rate limiting, error detail leakage, HTTP methods, and unsafe configuration.
Reports affected controls, evidence, severity, recommended fixes, and untested boundaries.
limitations: It does not prove production security or replace a penetration test.
It does not verify deployment TLS, reverse proxies, CDNs, WAFs, or certificates.
It does not scan dependencies, external infrastructure, or third-party identity providers.
It requires accurate routes, an importable application, and dedicated test credentials.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Application Review
use_cases.description: Run repeatable checks against a configured Python web application before a release decision.

use_cases.title: Security Regression Testing
use_cases.description: Add focused authentication, authorization, input, and configuration checks to a continuous integration workflow.

use_cases.title: Control Evidence Collection
use_cases.description: Document verified results, skipped checks, recommendations, and test boundaries for a security review.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my local Python web application with this skill. Identify the application import path, configure the required test values, run the suite, and summarize failures.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security suite to test authentication for my application. Check protected routes, invalid credentials, valid credentials, and account enumeration. Report evidence and skipped checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Authorization Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the suite to my configured authorization routes. Test object ownership, IDOR protections, role boundaries, and mass assignment. Separate application findings from infrastructure gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full configured security suite before release. Analyze every failure, verify route and threshold assumptions, document test boundaries, assign severity, recommend fixes, and provide a BLOCKED, REVIEW REQUIRED, or PASS decision.

output_examples.input: Run the configured suite against the local ASGI application and review the results.
output: Finding: The protected profile route returned success without valid authentication.
Evidence: The configured protected route accepted an unauthenticated request.
Recommendation: Enforce authentication before release and rerun the protected-route checks.

output_examples.input: Check whether the application leaks internal details through error responses.
output: Finding: An error response exposed internal configuration markers.
Severity: High because connection or secret details can support further attacks.
Boundary: The check covers the configured error route and does not verify production infrastructure.

output_examples.input: Generate a release summary after the configured checks finish.
output: Verified: Authentication, authorization, headers, CORS, cookies, rate limits, validation, errors, and methods.
Skipped: Any route or control not configured for the target application.
Decision: Review each failure with an owner before selecting a release gate.

best_practices: Use isolated environments, dedicated test accounts, and non-production data.
Configure actual routes and thresholds before interpreting failures.
Record skipped checks, verified evidence, severity, and application boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not use production credentials or production data during the audit.
Do not treat a passing configured suite as proof of complete security.
Do not classify an unconfigured route as secure because its check was skipped.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The suite targets FastAPI, Django, Flask with an ASGI adapter, and comparable ASGI applications.

faq.question: Does this perform a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It performs configured application-layer pytest checks and does not replace manual assessment or dynamic scanning.

faq.question: What credentials should I configure?
faq.answer: Use dedicated non-production user and administrator accounts. Keep the local .env.test file out of version control.

faq.question: Can it check production infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. Deployment TLS, proxies, CDNs, WAFs, certificates, dependencies, and external identity providers require separate review.

faq.question: What happens when a route is missing?
faq.answer: Configure route variables for the application. A skipped or unconfigured check is not evidence that the control passes.

faq.question: Does the suite test CSRF?
faq.answer: It does not provide a universal CSRF check. Add an application-specific test when state-changing requests use cookie authentication.
